chunks: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

The most deserving of the people to show humbleness in private and in public is the bearer of the Quran; and the most deserving of the people in private and in public for salat and fasting is the bearer of the Quran.

Then he called out in his loudest voice: 'O bearer of the Quran! Be humble with it and God will raise you, and do not seek glory through it or God will disgrace you. O bearer of the Quran! Adorn yourself with it for God's sake and God will adorn you with it; and do not adorn yourself with it for the people's sake or God will dishonor you with it.'

Whoever completes the Quran, it is as if prophethood has been placed within his sides — yet no revelation comes to him. And whoever memorizes the Quran, it befits him not to act ignorantly alongside those who act ignorantly toward him, not to become angry toward those who are angry with him, and not to be irritable toward those who are irritable with him — rather, he should pardon, excuse, forgive, and forbear, out of reverence for the Quran.

And whoever has been given the Quran, if he thinks that anyone from among the people has been given something superior to what he has been given, then he has magnified what God has belittled and belittled what God has magnified.

key_terms.التخشع: Al-takhashhu': profound humbleness and submissiveness before God, deeper than mere politeness
key_terms.النبوة: Al-nubuwwa: prophethood — the extraordinary spiritual state attributed metaphorically to Quran completion
key_terms.تواضع: Tawadu': voluntary humility, lowering oneself before God and others
key_terms.حامل القرآن: The bearer/memorizer of the Quran — one who has internalized the Quran in memory and practice
key_terms.يعفو ويصفح ويغفر ويحلم: The four virtues: pardoning, excusing, forgiving, and forbearing — all required of the Quran-bearer

ai.seo_question: What are the responsibilities of one who memorizes and bears the Quran according to a hadith of the Prophet?
ai.summary: The Prophet (SAWW) delivers a solemn exhortation directed at those who bear (memorize) the Quran, establishing them as having the highest responsibility for humbleness, salat, and fasting in both private and public life. Addressing bearers of the Quran directly with a raised voice, he teaches that the Quran must be used for sincerity toward God — as a means of adornment before God — and not for social prestige. The hadith culminates in a warning against undervaluing the Quran: treating it as merely equal to other gifts inverts divine values.
